boards.title: Your First Weekend at University of North Texas, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A low-key, under-21-safe sequence for getting oriented to UNT’s campus spaces, creative offerings, and recreation options.

cards.title: Start with a campus reset
cards.subtitle: University Union • 1155 Union Circle
cards.notes: Use the Union as an orientation stop: check the building map, find the information desk, and choose a comfortable place to regroup before exploring.
cards.short_summary: A central indoor stop for studying, dining, lounging, meetings, and campus services.
cards.evidence_claim: UNT describes the University Union as a facility for studying, socializing, lounging, dining, and meeting space.
cards.source_title: University Union | University of North Texas
cards.access_notes: Check current Union hours before visiting.

cards.title: See what students are making
cards.subtitle: Level 2, University Union
cards.notes: Walk behind the main information desk on Union level 2 and spend a few minutes with the current student-art exhibition; exhibition subjects rotate regularly.
cards.short_summary: A changing, student-focused exhibition space inside the Union.
cards.evidence_claim: The Union Art Gallery is on level 2, showcases UNT student creative work, and offers free exhibitions open to campus visitors.
cards.source_title: In The Union | University of North Texas
cards.access_notes: The gallery is open when the Union is open; verify Union hours before going.

cards.title: Make something during a drop-in
cards.subtitle: University Union, Room 214
cards.notes: Check the Union Arts Center’s current schedule, then drop in during open hours for its designated art activity or reserve a spot if a workshop requires it.
cards.short_summary: A permanent Union workshop space with drop-ins, workshops, and classes for enrolled students.
cards.evidence_claim: The Union Arts Center offers designated drop-in art activities, instructor-led workshops, and classes for currently enrolled UNT students.
cards.source_title: Union Arts Center | University of North Texas
cards.access_notes: Offerings and any fees vary; check the current schedule and eligibility before participating.

cards.title: Pause for a meal in the Union
cards.subtitle: University Union • Campus Chat Food Court
cards.notes: Use the official Union map to locate the Campus Chat Food Court, then choose among the listed vendors when you need a straightforward meal break.
cards.short_summary: A University Union food-court destination with several named dining counters.
cards.evidence_claim: UNT’s Union directory lists the Campus Chat Food Court and its food options, including Clark Bakery, Mia’s Pizza, Ramen Common, Sauté, Sushi, and Union Circle Salads & Sandwiches.
cards.access_notes: Dining availability and hours vary; confirm current Union dining hours.

cards.title: Choose a study-space base
cards.subtitle: Willis Library • UNT campus
cards.notes: Head to Willis Library and use the library’s study-space tools to find a setting that fits your plan, whether you want quiet focus or collaboration.
cards.short_summary: UNT’s main library location and a starting point for finding campus study areas.
cards.evidence_claim: UNT Libraries identifies Willis as a library location and directs visitors to its study-space finder and location details.
cards.access_notes: Review current library hours and any room-access requirements before visiting.

cards.title: Get your bearings outdoors
cards.subtitle: Outdoor area between the Union, ESSC, Hurley Administration Building, and Willis Library
cards.notes: Take a short walk through Library Mall to connect major campus buildings and note the routes you may use between the Union and Willis Library.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor campus area linking several central UNT destinations.
cards.evidence_claim: UNT identifies Library Mall as the outdoor area between the University Union/Eagle Student Service Center, Hurley Administration Building, and Willis Library.
cards.source_title: UNT Art Mart | University of North Texas
cards.access_notes: Outdoor access is weather-dependent; use normal campus pedestrian routes.

cards.title: Take a daylight breather
cards.subtitle: Level 4, University Union
cards.notes: Ride or walk up to Union level 4, then use Bruzzy’s Patio for a short outdoor pause before returning to your afternoon plans.
cards.short_summary: A level-4 Union patio named for UNT alumnus Jerome “Bruzzy” Westheimer.
cards.evidence_claim: UNT identifies Bruzzy’s Patio on level 4 of the Union and says it is a place for students to relax and get sun between classes.
cards.source_title: In The Union | University of North Texas
cards.access_notes: Use during Union operating hours and follow posted patio rules.

cards.title: Build in a quiet moment
cards.subtitle: Level 4, University Union
cards.notes: If you want a calmer stop, visit the Union’s Meditation Room and use the space briefly for quiet reflection before the next activity.
cards.short_summary: A designated quiet-reflection room featuring Norie Sato’s Quiet and Soaring artwork.
cards.evidence_claim: UNT says the Meditation Room is on level 4 of the Union, is open to the campus community, and is intended for reflection and destressing.
cards.source_title: In The Union | University of North Texas
cards.access_notes: Observe the room’s posted quiet-use guidelines and check Union access hours.

cards.title: Try a campus recreation option
cards.subtitle: 1900 Chestnut Street
cards.notes: Check the current recreation schedule, then plan a visit around an available activity such as the climbing wall, pools, courts, or indoor soccer gym.
cards.short_summary: UNT’s recreation facility with fitness, aquatics, climbing, courts, and outdoor-pursuits resources.
cards.evidence_claim: UNT lists a 45-foot climbing wall, two pools, and an indoor soccer gym among Pohl Recreation Center recreation options.
cards.source_title: Campus Life | The UNT Experience | University of North Texas
cards.access_notes: Current summer 2026 Pohl Rec Center hours include Sunday 12–10 p.m., Monday–Thursday 6 a.m.–10 p.m., Friday 6 a.m.–9 p.m., and Saturday 8 a.m.–7 p.m.; membership or eligibility may apply.

cards.title: End with a garden walk
cards.subtitle: UNT Community Garden • UNT campus
cards.notes: Visit the garden as a slower final stop and look over the raised plots; if you want to participate beyond observing, review the garden-member application details.
cards.short_summary: A collaborative-learning garden with raised plots growing produce, herbs, flowers, and fruit.
cards.evidence_claim: UNT describes the Community Garden as a collaborative-learning space with 20 raised plots growing organic vegetables, fruits, herbs, and flowers.
cards.source_title: Physical Wellness | University of North Texas
cards.access_notes: Garden plots are managed by members; consult the program before entering or using a plot.
